definitions.explanation: The act of taking control of a territory, area, or position by military force. Also used figuratively for monopolizing a space.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}に{占領|せんりょう}された。
examples.english: It was occupied by the enemy.

examples.japanese: {戦後|せんご}、{日本|にほん}は{連合国|れんごうこく}に{占領|せんりょう}された。
examples.english: After the war, Japan was occupied by the Allied forces.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちがソファを{占領|せんりょう}していて{座|すわ}れない。
examples.english: The kids have taken over the sofa and I can't sit down.

notes:
Also functions as a する verb ({占領|せんりょう}する). In modern Japanese, sometimes used humorously for 'taking over' a space (example 3).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{軍事|ぐんじ}{占領|せんりょう} — military occupation
・{占領|せんりょう}{下|か} — under occupation
・{占領|せんりょう}{軍|ぐん} — occupation forces
・{占領|せんりょう}{地|ち} — occupied territory

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{征服|せいふく} — conquest (complete subjugation)
・{侵略|しんりゃく} — invasion, aggression
・{支配|しはい} — domination, control
